title: Your first words
goal: A one-syllable word is one stroke: the sounds it starts with, its vowel, the sounds it ends with. Say it, split it, strike it.

blocks.x: Say it, split it, strike it

items: Say the word slowly. Find the **vowel sound**.
What comes before it? Those are left-hand keys (lesson 3).
What comes after? Those are right-hand keys (lessons 5 and 6).
Strike all of it at once.

blocks.x: No vowel in your head? Say the word and **feel** where it opens your mouth: that is the vowel. A word with no start or no end just leaves that hand off ([[at|AT]], [[out|OUT]]).

blocks.title: Say it, split it, strike it
blocks.x: Five to start with. The keys light up after a miss.
You are not memorising a word list here. You are learning to **derive** a stroke from a sound. That skill is what you fall back on for any word you have not memorised.

If everything fits in steno order, it is one stroke. A word with two or more syllables usually needs more: you will build those with the join key from lesson 10. Many common ones already have a memorised one-stroke form, which is next.
